title: König's theorem (kinetics)
source_statement_excerpt: In kinematics, König's theorem or König's decomposition is a mathematical relation derived by Johann Samuel König that assists with the calculations of angular momentum and kinetic energy of bodies and systems of particles.
statement: A system of finitely many particles of masses $m_i$ has positions $r_i$, velocities $v_i$, center-of-mass position $R$, and center-of-mass velocity $V$ in an inertial frame. Its angular momentum about the origin decomposes as $L=R\times\sum_i m_iV+L'$, where $L'$ is angular momentum relative to the center of mass.

title: Kac's lemma
source_statement_excerpt: In ergodic theory, Kac's lemma, demonstrated by mathematician Mark Kac in 1947, is a lemma stating that in a finite measure space the orbit of almost all the points contained in a set $A$ of such space, whose measure is $\mu (A)$ , return to $A$ within an average time inversely proportional to $\mu (A)$ .
statement: $(X,\mathcal B,\mu,T)$ is an ergodic probability-preserving dynamical system, and $A\in\mathcal B$ satisfies $\mu(A)>0$. For the first return time $\tau_A(x)=\min\{k\ge1:T^k x\in A\}$, $E(\tau_A\mid x\in A)=1/\mu(A)$.
